fixes.explanation: No "come back tomorrow" here, friend. There's no tomorrow anywhere in what God says. He says, "As surely as I live, I will not be consulted by you…" (Ezekiel 20:3). The answer is no, and He swears to it.

That's the one. God says it was because "…their hearts continually went after their idols." (Ezekiel 20:16). That's where their hearts kept going, and notice the word continually. It's the reason God gives for the oath.

Their own statutes isn't what God says, friend. He says, "I am the LORD your God; walk in My statutes, keep My ordinances, and practice them." (Ezekiel 20:19). The statutes He points to are His, not theirs.

That's what the text says. "…they saw any high hill or leafy tree, there they offered their sacrifices…" (Ezekiel 20:28). They also presented offerings, sent up incense and poured out drink offerings. Those are the places the verse names.
The text says the opposite. They offered their sacrifices where they saw any high hill or leafy tree (Ezekiel 20:28). The verse names a hill and a tree, and no altar. So that answer doesn't fit.

The verse says the opposite. These offerings "provoked Me" (Ezekiel 20:28). They were offered where the fathers saw any high hill or leafy tree, with incense and drink offerings too. The word God uses is provoked.
Bethel isn't the name this verse gives, friend. It says, "(And to this day it is called Bamah.)" (Ezekiel 20:29). Bamah is the name that stuck for the high place.

Gilgal sounds right, I'll give you that, and I've confidently guessed worse myself. But the verse says, "(And to this day it is called Bamah.)" (Ezekiel 20:29). Bamah is what the high place was called.

Reaching for the sky there, friend, but the verse stays closer to the ground. What they say is, "…serving wood and stone…" (Ezekiel 20:32). Sun and moon aren't mentioned. Wood and stone are what they'd be serving.

That's what He says. "…I will bring you into the wilderness of the nations, where I will enter into judgment with you face to face." (Ezekiel 20:35). Face to face is the phrase God uses. It's a judgment meeting in the wilderness of the nations.

A pillar of fire isn't mentioned in this passage, friend. What God says is that He will enter into judgment with them face to face in the wilderness of the nations (Ezekiel 20:35). The verse names judgment there, not a pillar.

That's the spot. God says, "For on My holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there the whole house of Israel, all of them, will serve Me in the land." (Ezekiel 20:40). He says it about the whole house of Israel, all of them. His holy mountain is the place.

Egypt is where they started, friend, but that's not where this promise lands. God says, "For on My holy mountain, the high mountain of Israel…there the whole house of Israel, all of them, will serve Me in the land." (Ezekiel 20:40). The place is His holy mountain.

Aroma is right. God says, "…I will accept you as a pleasing aroma." (Ezekiel 20:41). That promise comes when He brings them from the peoples and gathers them from the lands where they were scattered. Pleasing is the word He uses.

That's what the text says. "There you will remember your ways and all the deeds with which you have defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have done." (Ezekiel 20:43). It's a heavy line. The remembering and the loathing are both right there in the same verse.
Careful isn't the word, baker. God says, "…not according to your wicked ways and corrupt acts…" (Ezekiel 20:44). He deals with them for the sake of His name.
